Container.Name: CamStack-Agent
Container.Overview: A CamStack Agent is a worker node. It joins a CamStack hub and runs the heavy work on this machine instead: ML detection, hardware decode/encode, the WebRTC and RTSP broker, and recording. This is not a standalone install — run the CamStack hub first, then point this at it. The agent is paired from the hub: open Cluster → Nodes, find it under Agents found on the network (or add it by address) and confirm the same six-digit code on the hub and on the agent's own page on port 4444. There is no shared secret to copy; after pairing the agent and hub trust each other by certificate. The app version is managed by the hub; only the boot loader comes from this image.
Container.Requires: A running CamStack hub on the same network — set its address below.

Config.Name: Status dashboard (HTTP)
Config.Description: Agent status dashboard: hub connection, cameras handled here, logs and metrics. Also where you pick the hub to join when no hub address is set.

Config.Name: Cluster mesh (mTLS)
Config.Description: Mutual-TLS listener the hub reaches this agent on once it has joined. Keep it on your LAN and never forward it. The old clear ports (6000 and the 20000-29999 range) and the UDP discovery port 4445 are retired.

Config.Name: RTSP restream
Config.Description: RTSP restream served on demand by the stream broker.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Installed addons, ML models, native dependencies, logs and this agent's identity. Use a different folder from the hub. Safe to wipe — it re-seeds from the hub on the next boot.

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: config.yaml. The image declares /config as a volume, so leaving it unmapped makes Docker create a fresh anonymous volume on every re-create. Map it even though an agent keeps little here.

Config.Name: Backups
Config.Description: The image declares /backups as a volume. An agent rarely runs backup destinations, but map it (or Docker makes a fresh anonymous volume on every re-create). Paired with CAMSTACK_BACKUP_ROOT.

Config.Name: Recordings
Config.Description: Recordings and event media for cameras assigned to this agent. Point at a roomy share. Paired with CAMSTACK_MEDIA_ROOT below.

Config.Name: Intel/AMD iGPU
Config.Description: Optional. Enter /dev/dri to pass the integrated GPU: hardware video decode (VAAPI/QSV) and OpenVINO GPU or ONNX WebGPU inference. Leave empty if the machine has none; software decode costs roughly 60% of a CPU for a handful of 4K HEVC cameras.

Config.Name: Intel NPU / AMD XDNA
Config.Description: Optional. Enter /dev/accel to pass an Intel NPU (Core Ultra, OpenVINO NPU inference). An AMD XDNA NPU is detected but has no inference runtime yet. Leave empty if the machine has no NPU.

Config.Name: Coral USB (whole USB bus)
Config.Description: Optional. Enter /dev/bus/usb for a Coral USB Edge TPU. Mapped as a path (the whole bus), not a device, because the stick re-enumerates from 1a6e:089a to 18d1:9302 when libedgetpu initialises; the device-cgroup-rule in Extra Parameters admits the new node. The node must also be writable by CamStack: add the udev rule from the Unraid install guide (Coral USB section).

Config.Name: Coral PCIe/M.2 unit 1
Config.Description: Optional. Enter /dev/apex_0 for a PCIe or M.2 Coral Edge TPU. Needs the gasket/apex driver on the Unraid host (the Coral driver plugin in Community Applications); ls -l /dev/apex_* on the host must list it. Requires an image newer than v1.2.583.

Config.Name: Coral PCIe/M.2 unit 2
Config.Description: Optional. Enter /dev/apex_1 for a second PCIe/M.2 Coral (a dual-TPU card shows as two units). Same host driver as unit 1; each unit is its own inference device in CamStack.

Config.Name: Node role
Config.Description: hub | agent. One image serves both; this selects the role at boot. Leave it as agent here.

Config.Name: Hub address
Config.Description: IP or hostname of the hub to join, e.g. 192.168.x.x. Leave blank and the agent stays unconfigured: open the dashboard on port 4444, pair it from the hub (Cluster → Nodes → Agents found on the network, found over mDNS, which needs host networking or br0) or add it by address, then confirm the six-digit code on both screens.

Config.Name: Hub URL
Config.Description: Full hub base URL, e.g. https://192.168.x.x:4443. Leave blank to derive it from the hub address above; set it only when the hub is on a non-default port or behind a proxy.

Config.Name: Node ID
Config.Description: Stable cluster identifier for this agent, e.g. gpu-box. Defaults to the container hostname. Must be unique across the cluster and must not change once the hub knows it.

Config.Name: Display name
Config.Description: How this agent is labelled in the topology view. Defaults to the node ID.

Config.Name: Media root
Config.Description: Container path all media is written under. Must match the Recordings path above.

Config.Name: Cluster: advertise hostname
Config.Description: Must stay false for a multi-machine cluster so nodes advertise their IP rather than a container hostname no other host can resolve.

Config.Name: Log level
Config.Description: trace | debug | info | warn | error.
